paper.title: Language to Rewards for Robotic Skill Synthesis
paper.central_claim: Language to Rewards uses LLMs to translate natural-language user instructions and feedback into reward functions, enabling a general model-predictive controller to synthesize diverse robot skills and refine them through interaction, including sim-to-real demonstrations.

evidence.quote: A Motion Descriptor LLM takes the user input and describe the user-specified motion in natural language, and a Reward Coder translates the motion into the reward parameters.
evidence.support_explanation: Two-stage language-to-reward interface, not arbitrary low-level policy generation.

evidence.quote: is a twice-differentiable norm that takes its minimum at 0
evidence.support_explanation: Hand-designed smooth residual family with weights/parameters; language selects within family.

evidence.quote: For each task and method considered, we generate 10 responses from Reward Translator, each evaluated in MJPC for 50 times, thus we measure the end-to-end stability of the full pipeline.
evidence.support_explanation: 10 code samples×50 controller trials per task/method; code-sample and rollout variance are distinct.

evidence.quote: For each point in the plot, it represents the percentage of tasks the system can solve, given that it can generate N pieces of code for each task and pick the best performing one.
evidence.support_explanation: Pass curve includes best-code selection; not single-shot autonomous robot SR or disjoint postselection test.

signatures.object: Language instruction to parameterized reward artifact
signatures.information: User instruction, morphology-specific hand-authored motion-description template, fixed residual API definitions and examples; simulator state privileged. GPT4 translates language, no trained VLA.
signatures.operation: Motion Descriptor fills natural-language motion schema; Reward Coder emits API calls/weights/targets for predefined residuals; build negative weighted smooth residual norm reward.
signatures.conditions: Desired behavior representable by residual family, adequate template/API semantics and controller dynamics/model.
signatures.feedback: Interactive user corrections revise descriptions/reward; generated-code rollout assessment used for evaluation, not autonomous semantic approval.
signatures.selection_rule: Evaluation generatesN candidates and selects best performance; human interaction supplies revision intent.
signatures.selection_data: 17 simulation task categories and rollout trials; no independent holdout after best-code selection established.
signatures.persistence: Task-specific reward parameters; no growing cross-task executable library or retained harness improvement claim.
signatures.later_use: Controller replans using reward at runtime; user can request updates.
signatures.claimed_effect: Better skill coverage/stability than direct reward coding or finite primitive composition.
signatures.failure_boundary: Hand-designed template/residual expressivity, physically invalid/extreme targets and selection bias; not arbitrary reward invention.

signatures.object: Model-predictive motion synthesis and hardware adaptation
signatures.information: Current robot state/dynamics; iLQG for12DoF quadruped and predictive sampling for27DoF manipulator. Real F-VLM masks/point clouds/AprilTag table calibration replace ground-truth objects.
signatures.operation: Repeated receding-horizon MJPC optimization under generated reward; sim2real regularization restricts unstable motion.
signatures.output: Closed-loop robot controls, physical pushing/grasping demonstrations.
signatures.conditions: Accurate state/model, stable controller, feasible reward and real perception/calibration.
signatures.feedback: State feedback improves motion; it does not certify linguistic task intent or semantic correctness.
signatures.selection_rule: MPC selects controls by objective; user/code selection selects objective, not autonomous validated self-improvement.
signatures.selection_data: 50 rollouts/code sample simulation; two physical task types without complete denominators.
signatures.persistence: Fixed controller and per-task reward; no learned policy or cross-task accumulated self-improvement.
signatures.later_use: Online reoptimization from new robot states.
signatures.claimed_effect: Flexible skill synthesis and sim2real applicability.
signatures.failure_boundary: Physical demo not counted transfer-grade SR; additional regularization/perception means not unchanged transfer.

gap.author_gap: LLM primitive sequencing is restricted by hand-authored skill coverage, while direct language-to-motor commands lack control precision.
gap.checked_gap: Reward-mediated continuous optimization extends beyond primitive sequences; reward family/templates remain hand-designed and controller/model quality is prerequisite.

claims.text: Broad and stable language-driven skill synthesis
claims.setting: 9 quadruped+8 manipulation simulation task categories; GPT4/MJPC
claims.baseline_control: Direct Reward Coder without descriptor; CaP with designed primitive set; full prompts in appendices.
claims.selection_vs_test: 10 reward-code samples/method/task,50rollouts each; coverage curve selects best amongN. No independent selection/test split shown.
claims.result_denominator: 17 categories,10codes×50rollouts/task/method; improvement11/17 categories. Roughly90% vs50% converged task coverage is best-code task coverage, not first-attempt SR.
counterevidence: Shared predefined residual family limits behavior set.
Different primitive expressivity; no full factorial prompt/model/budget control.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Parameterized rewards plus MPC give better sampled-code coverage in these tasks; not a90% autonomous robot success rate.
